title: Prompt injection
point: Any text the model reads can try to act as an instruction, so defend with structure that treats untrusted text as data, not with more instructions.
definition: Prompt injection is text that tries to change an agent's behaviour against its principal's intent. Direct injection comes from the person typing; indirect injection hides inside content the agent reads, such as pages, emails, files or tool results.

objective.text: Classify an attack as direct or indirect, explain why instruction-only defences are not enough, and choose structural defences such as quarantine, typed outputs, allowlists and gateway authorisation.

misconceptions.claim: Adding a line telling the model to ignore instructions in documents prevents indirect injection.
misconceptions.correction: It may lower the success rate of some attacks, but it guarantees nothing. The model reads one stream of tokens and cannot reliably tell your instructions from an attacker's.

misconceptions.claim: Only the user can inject prompts, so authenticating users makes the agent safe.
misconceptions.correction: Indirect injection arrives through content, not the chat box. A trusted user who asks for a summary of a hostile web page delivers the attacker's text for them.

l1: Direct injection: the person typing tries to override the agent, for example by asking it to reveal its system prompt or skip a policy check.
Indirect injection: instructions hidden in content the agent reads, such as hidden text on a web page, a line in an inbound email or a poisoned tool description.
The model cannot reliably separate instructions from data in its context. Defences must therefore limit what a successful injection can do, not only try to prevent it.
l2: Treat untrusted text as data. Pass it to a quarantined model call with no tools that returns only schema-validated fields, such as an intent enum and an order number.
Use typed outputs and allowlists. If the next step accepts only an order ID that matches a pattern, an injected sentence has nowhere to go.
Authorise in the gateway and the database under the principal's identity. An injected refund request then fails at authorisation, whatever the model was persuaded to propose.
l3: Measure rather than assume. Keep a test set of hostile emails and pages, and track the attack success rate for each release alongside task accuracy.
Expect a non-zero bypass rate from model-level defences such as classifiers and tuned refusals. Use structure to bound the remaining blast radius, so a 1 per cent bypass cannot leak data.
Watch the quarantine boundary. A free-text summary field lets injected text ride through to the planner, so prefer enums, numbers and IDs.
